transcript.text: f/f freezer keeps icing up bottom drawer wont shut proper, defrosted it 2wks ago already full of ice again. indesit

I understand you've already defrosted it two weeks ago and it has iced up again. This rapid recurrence suggests an automatic defrost system fault rather than just user error (like leaving the door open). In a frost-free fridge-freezer, if the heater, thermostat or sensor fails, ice builds up on the evaporator coils behind the rear panel. This blocks airflow, causing the freezer to get very cold and icy while the fridge section may go warm, and excess meltwater can freeze in the bottom drawer area. Before we look at internal parts, I need to confirm exactly where the ice is. Please unplug the appliance for safety. Empty the freezer and remove any shelves or drawers that prevent you seeing the back wall inside the freezer compartment. Once you have access:
1. Look at the rear panel/coils: Is it a solid block of white ice, or fairly clear?
2. Look at the bottom of that back wall for a small drain hole: Is it visible and clear, blocked by debris/ice, or hidden under ice? Please describe what you see. This will tell us if we are dealing with a failed defrost component (requiring part replacement) or a simple blockage.
its not frost free tho, its a manual defrost one. ice is mostly round the front edge and bottom drawer, thick frost. not sure about a drain hole, cant see one

Thanks for clarifying it’s a manual defrost model. Since you’ve already done a full defrost and it iced up again within two weeks, we need to find out why moisture is getting back in. The most common cause of rapid re-icing in manual freezers is warm air leaking in through the door seal (gasket). If the rubber is torn, dirty or folded, every time you open the door, humid kitchen air enters and turns into thick frost. Please unplug the appliance for safety. Empty the freezer and look closely at the rubber door seal. Is there any tear, split or section where the rubber has come away from the plastic frame? Also, is the seal dirty or folded in a way that stops it sealing tightly?
ok looked. bottom corner of the freezer door seal is split about 5cm and the hinge side bottom bit is flattened. not dirty or folded otherwise. fridge seal is fine

[Heading: Likely cause: door seal]
That split in the seal is probably why your freezer iced up again so quickly. A 5cm gap lets warm kitchen air straight into the freezer every time you open the door; that moisture turns to thick frost very fast, which explains why the bottom drawer won’t shut properly. The good news is this is a straightforward fix: replacing the freezer door seal (gasket). To make sure we get the right part for your Indesit fridge-freezer, I just need the model number. It’s usually on a sticker inside the appliance, often on a side wall or near the salad drawer. Once you have that, I can tell you exactly which seal to order and how to fit it safely.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
its IB55532W, indesit. read it off the rating plate

[Heading: Likely cause: door seal]
That split in the seal is most likely why your freezer iced up again so quickly. A 5cm gap lets warm kitchen air straight into the freezer every time you open the door; that moisture turns to thick frost very fast, which explains why the bottom drawer won’t shut properly. The good news is this is a straightforward fix: replacing the freezer door seal (gasket). To make sure we get the right part for your Indesit IB55532W fridge-freezer, I need you to order it directly from an authorised Indesit spares supplier or visit the manufacturer's official parts website. They will have the exact gasket for this model. When fitting it:
1. Pull the old seal out of its groove in the door frame carefully.
2. Clean the groove thoroughly so no debris stops the new one sitting flat.
3. Press the new seal into place, starting at the top corner and working your way down both sides to the bottom, ensuring it sits evenly all around.
4. Once fitted, close the door and check that it shuts firmly with even pressure along the whole edge. After replacing the seal, you should find the icing stops completely. If you have any trouble finding the correct part for this specific model number, I recommend contacting Indesit customer support or a qualified appliance engineer to source and fit it for you.
